newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius Rogers bonds issue oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius Rogers bonds issue oversubscribed.

text.p: The sale of 200 million rupees ($10 million) in secured bonds by conglomerate Rogers raised 530 million rupees from the public.

Company Secretary Andre Raffray said in a statement on Wednesday: "In addition to the 50 million rupees which were privately placed with five commercial banks, over 700 applications for a total amount of 530 million rupees were received."
He added: "The company has therefore decided to exercise its right to retain 50 million rupees of oversubscriptions, thereby bringing the total amount of applications accepted to 250 million rupees."
The extra 280 million rupees will be paid back to the applicants who took part in the bonds sale, he said.
The Rogers bonds have a coupon rate of 10.5 percent, and were sold in a public offer from March 11 to 20 last. They mature in March 2002 but early redemption can occur as from March 2000.

The 250 million rupees raised will be used to finance Rogers' ventures in areas such as the freeport, leasing, paint production, warehousing and bottling facilities. The bonds will be quoted on the Stock Exchange of Mauritius in April.

In the financial year to 30 September 1996, Rogers profit before tax slipped to 423.7 million rupees from 428.6 million in 1995. Turnover of was posted at 8.67 billion rupees in 1995/96 up from 7.97 billion in 1994/95.
Rogers has forecast profits before tax at 490 million rupees for the current financial year ($ = 20.09 Mauritius Rupees)
